intro: Benin was home to the Kingdom of Dahomey, famous for its women soldiers, and is the birthplace of the Vodun religion.

chapters.title: The Kingdom of Dahomey
text: Dahomey, ruled from Abomey from the 1600s, became a powerful kingdom. Its kings' palaces are now a World Heritage site. It had an all-female army, the Agojie, whom Europeans called 'Amazons'.
Dahomey grew rich by selling captives into the Atlantic slave trade through Ouidah.

highlight.title: The Agojie
highlight.text: Women warriors who fought for Dahomey into the 1890s.

chapters.title: French Dahomey
text: France defeated King Béhanzin and conquered Dahomey in 1894. It became independent in 1960 and was renamed Benin in 1975.

chapters.title: Democracy
text: After a Marxist government, Benin held a national conference in 1990 that peacefully brought in democracy, a model copied elsewhere in Africa. In 2021 France returned 26 royal treasures looted from Abomey.

keyTerms.meaning: A religion from West Africa, origin of Haitian Vodou.
